newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends sharply lower on poor export demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends sharply lower on poor export demand.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended sharply lower with the May contract near the 30 cent per cwt lower limit on poor USDA weekly export sales figures and weak cash demand, traders said.
"There hasn't been any demand," a trader said. "This (USDA) sales report shows we can't sell any rice."
USDA on Thursday pegged weekly sales at 18,600 tonnes, down 51 percent from the previous week.
The market awaited results of Costa Rica's 30,000 tonne rice tender. Trade sources expected Costa Rica to buy some U.S. supplies but thought the majority would be Argentine.

Bulls continued to watch wet weather in Texas rice growing regions. They cited a six- to 10-day outlook calling for above normal precipitation in the U.S. south. Texas was still drying out from recent heavy rains that will likely delay plantings, traders said.
Rice closed 27 to three cents per cwt lower with May down 27 at $11.35.
Thursday's volume was estimated by CBOT at 550 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 442 lots.
